title: Trump: Democrats' unity against Trump faces a test after U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran
description_short: A PBS/AP report described divisions among Democrats over the Iran strikes, a pending war-powers vote, and debate over Israel policy.
description_medium: An Associated Press report published by PBS on March 3, 2026, said Democrats had largely stayed aligned in opposing Trump’s immigration tactics and criticizing his economic policies and ties to Jeffrey Epstein. U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran tested that unity: party leaders urged a war-powers vote, while several Democrats objected to the measure or rejected claims the attack was illegal. The report also described renewed debate over Israel and AIPAC in party primaries.
description_long: Published March 3, 2026, the PBS NewsHour page carried an Associated Press report on whether Democrats could maintain unity after U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran. It said Democrats had recently coalesced around opposition to Trump’s immigration tactics and criticized his economic policies and ties to Jeffrey Epstein. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer called for a quick war-powers resolution to limit Trump’s options. Some Democrats, including Rep. Greg Landsman, Rep. Josh Gottheimer and Sen. John Fetterman, expressed reservations or opposed the measure; Fetterman also rejected arguments that the attack was illegal. The report connected these disagreements to a wider party debate over Israel and noted that the affiliated super PAC of the American Israel Public Affairs Committee had opposed New Jersey primary candidate Tom Malinowski before progressive candidate Analilia Mejia won the primary. The article describes a test of Democratic cohesion and disputes over war powers and Israel policy; it does not report the outcome of a final congressional vote.
notes: The linked PBS page was read directly and supplies the date, the named lawmakers and positions, the proposed war-powers vote, and the Israel/AIPAC primary context. The revised account is limited to the debate the report describes and does not assert a final vote or downstream outcome.
